files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller's checklist

Owner: E. Nakamura. Complete in sequence; no shortcuts.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, propose one correcting journal entry.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months, every run pays in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule and supporting contracts. Check the GL first to avoid a duplicate. If the entry is missing, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry. Apply the convention that a full month is taken in the month a prepaid item begins.
4. Book June depreciation per the fixed asset register, after first verifying what is already recorded in the GL.
5. Check the June vendor-bill documents against the GL, verify that each expense is coded to the correct account, and reclass anything miscoded.
6. After items 1-5 are booked, prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Ironline Distributors Inc. began in 2014 when two former warehouse colleagues saw that local businesses needed a dependable source for everyday operating supplies without the complexity of dealing with multiple manufacturers. They started with a modest catalog and a borrowed corner of a shared warehouse, building the company through practical service, careful purchasing, and word-of-mouth referrals.

Today, Ironline Distributors Inc. is a small wholesale business supplying packaging materials, shipping consumables, workplace essentials, and light industrial goods to food producers, laboratories, agencies, and other commercial customers. Its role is straightforward: consolidate routine orders, keep useful stock close at hand, and get products where they need to go with minimal fuss.

The team has a hands-on character. Sales staff know the warehouse flow, warehouse staff recognize regular customers, and the accounting desk is accustomed to resolving questions by walking over and asking. The culture favors plain language, tidy paperwork, and practical fixes over elaborate process.

The company remains an ordinary going concern, serving its established customer base while refining its product mix and vendor relationships. Current priorities include improving fulfillment consistency, clarifying expense coding, refreshing customer outreach, and making the month-end close more repeatable as the business continues to mature.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Keep the Ironline Distributors Inc. message practical: dependable wholesale supply, responsive people, and fewer headaches for customers managing routine purchasing.

## Priorities

- Refresh the brand voice and core sales materials without losing the straightforward, established feel customers recognize.
- Run two useful webinars per quarter, centered on inventory planning, packaging choices, and smoother replenishment workflows.
- Pilot a co-marketing program with selected supplier partners. Favor educational content and customer examples over generic promotion.
- Build a repeatable email rhythm for current customers, lapsed accounts, and qualified prospects.
- Give sales a compact set of product sheets and follow-up templates that can be adapted by industry.
- Capture more customer feedback from routine service conversations and turn recurring themes into content.

## Quarterly emphasis

**Q3:** Complete messaging work, update priority materials, launch the webinar series, and select partners for the pilot.

**Q4:** Expand the strongest campaigns, publish practical customer stories, and review which channels are producing worthwhile conversations.

## Measures

Track webinar attendance, sales follow-up, partner participation, email engagement, repeat inquiries, and qualified opportunities. Review results jointly with sales and operations so campaigns reflect available products and realistic fulfillment capacity.

Budget remains pending Q2 close.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from the previous accountant

E. Nakamura — a few things I learned the hard way:

- The bank tends to place its own fees and charges near the end of the statement. We normally pick those up during close rather than booking them throughout the month, so read all the way down.
- I was moving quickly in June, and the expense coding on one or two vendor bills may be wrong. Treat the source documents in `bills/` as authoritative and adjust the GL to match them.
- The budget was fixed early in Q2. The one-off June items were not planned, and they should explain most of the larger budget-to-actual variances.
- Please do not guess on payroll timing. The pay date for the second monthly run varies; check the payroll register before deciding whether an accrual is needed.
